repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for every changed schema: add optional column tags to ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, optional column classification to metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and the metadata-graph Column schema, the new classification PUT endpoint, masked_columns on the entitlements Decision, and masking metadata on the query response; released as minor 2.4.0.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Typed clients drop undeclared fields (ADR-004) and publish validation pins a contracts release, so the SDK must pin contracts 2.4.0, add classification to the MetadataClient Column model, add a set-classification method, and add masked_columns to the EntitlementsClient Decision model.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Postgres connectors already read column comments such as 'tags: pii,email' but do not propagate them; they must parse the tags and publish them as an optional columns[].tags field on ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 (AC1).

repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owning service: store classification per column node, suggest it from ingested tags without overwriting steward overrides, expose it on GET columns and a new steward PUT endpoint, and include it in metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (AC1, AC2).

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: Strict consumer that validates metadata.dataset.changed.v1 against a vendored contracts 2.1.0 schema with additionalProperties false, so it must re-vendor the 2.4.0 schema and deploy before metadata-graph emits column classification or every change event goes to the DLQ.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: The only place access decisions are computed (ADR-007); it must load column classifications from metadata-graph, check the requester's pii:read grant, and return masked_columns on POST /v1/access/decide (AC3), with its cache invalidated on classification changes.

repositories.name: query-gateway
repositories.reason: The single enforcement point that returns data to consumers (ADR-007); it must read masked_columns from the decision and mask those columns in POST /v1/query results (AC4).

repositories.name: dq-engine
repositories.reason: Picks rules per column by data type today; it must read classification from MetadataClient.get_columns (SDK bump) and bind PII-format validation rules to columns classified PII (AC5).

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: New cross-service behaviour (tag -> classification -> masked decision -> masked query result, and PII DQ rules) needs a new end-to-end suite run in the int environment per the change playbook.

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Tolerant consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 that reads only dataset.urn and dataset.name, so it needs only a contract-test rerun against the 2.4.0 payload.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Reads only owner from GET /v1/datasets/{urn} via the SDK and dq.result.published.v1 tolerantly; neither shape changes in a breaking way, so re-run its tests (and after any SDK bump).

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes only gateway.access.logged.v1 (principal, dataset_urn, row_count), which this plan does not change.

considered_not_impacted.name: reporting-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Decommissioned and archived in 2025; the mention in the metadata-graph README is stale, so it does not consume metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

considered_not_impacted.name: platform-catalog
considered_not_impacted.reason: No new component, topic or API-level dependency edge is created (entitlements-service already consumes metadata-graph-api); only optional description updates.

considered_not_impacted.name: architecture-docs
considered_not_impacted.reason: Documentation only; flows and the consumer registry should be updated after rollout, but no code or tests depend on it.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lowercase strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. ["pii","email"]); stays on .v1 with platform-contracts 2.4.0.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (enum PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII) and optional dataset.columns[].classification_source (enum SUGGESTED|STEWARD); classification changes are published with the existing COLUMNS_CHANGED change_type, no new enum value. Additive under ADR-009 but breaks strict search-indexer until it re-vendors the schema.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Column schema gains optional classification and classification_source (nullable when unclassified); metadata-graph-api 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets or overrides a column classification: body {classification, reason?}; returns the updated Column; 400 on invalid value, 404 on unknown dataset/column, 403 without steward permission; records classification_source STEWARD and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (COLUMNS_CHANGED).

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decide
contracts.description: Decision gains optional masked_columns (array of column names, empty when the principal holds pii:read or no column is PII); request body unchanged; entitlements-api 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0.

contracts.name: POST /v1/query
contracts.description: Values of columns listed in the decision's masked_columns are masked in rows (key kept, value replaced by null, assumption) and the response gains optional masked_columns so consumers can tell masked from real nulls; behind a flag; query-api 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0.

open_questions: Mapping from source tags to classification: is 'pii' (and pii sub-tags such as email/phone/ssn) the only PII trigger, and which tags map to CONFIDENTIAL/INTERNAL/PUBLIC? Assumed: any of pii,email,phone,ssn,name,address -> PII; 'confidential' -> CONFIDENTIAL; 'public' -> PUBLIC; otherwise no suggestion (null).
Is a suggested (not steward-confirmed) PII classification enforced for masking immediately? Assumed yes (fail closed); stewards can downgrade.
How should unclassified columns be treated: as INTERNAL for masking purposes (not masked) or masked until classified? Assumed not masked, to avoid a breaking change for existing consumers.

Is pii:read a global grant or scoped per domain/dataset in entitlements-service, and who administers it? Assumed it is a new grant type resolvable via the existing grants model, scope per domain to be confirmed with team-access.
Masking format: null vs a type-preserving token vs a redaction string like '***'? Assumed null plus masked_columns to keep column types stable for typed consumers.

How does query-gateway handle masked columns used inside expressions, aliases, joins, WHERE or GROUP BY (e.g. SELECT upper(email) AS e)? Masking by output column name alone could leak; needs SQL column-lineage resolution or rejection of such queries.
Should CONFIDENTIAL columns also be masked for some principals, or is masking only for PII in this ticket? Assumed PII only.
Who may call the classification PUT endpoint (steward role source and auth mechanism for metadata-graph) and should changes be audited beyond the change event?

Is classification configured for DQ via the dq-api /v1/rules bindings (a new classification selector on POST /v1/rules) or internally in dq-engine? Assumed internal dq-engine default bindings plus an optional additive selector later.
Backfill: existing datasets have no tags until re-ingested; should ingestion re-run schema discovery for all Postgres sources, and who owns the backfill?
Should gateway.access.logged.v1 carry masked_columns for audit? Not included here to keep usage-metering untouched.

Should search-indexer index/filter by classification, or just accept the field? Assumed accept and optionally index; also, can search-indexer move to tolerant reading to avoid this coupling in future?
Entitlements cache staleness: if a classification change event is delayed or lost, PII could be served unmasked; is a cache TTL acceptable as a backstop?
